catalog_quote: Der Akzent ist unbeweglich; er ruht immer auf derselben Silbe in allen Formen und zum Teil auch Ableitungen eines Wortes: mál Berg, best. máli, gen. dat. plur. máleve ... Seiner Stelle nach steht der Akzent in Grundwörtern auf der letzten Silbe und nur in ganz bestimmten Fällen auch auf der vorletzten. Diese letzteren betreffen Feminina auf -ə, -e (aus -jā = -jə) und -o: púnə (pu'n) Arbeit, núse Braut, víto Taube; Adjektiva, sowie überhaupt Wörter auf -ə: i bárδə (i ba'rδ) weiß, part. pírə (pī) getrunken ...; Suffixe -əs, -ən, -zə, -ur, -un, -tə, -tas, -a, -əń (-ij): vjéδəs Dieb, ... čúpəzə demin. Mädchen, i búkur schön ... Alle übrigen Grundwörter und Suffixe sind oxytoniert: kunát Schwager, čobán Hirt, besník der Treue ... kərkój suche, gənéj lüge, godís treffe ... Mit Ausnahme der oben angeführten Ausnahmen gehören hieher also vor allem alle Masculina und Verba, während die Domäne der Paroxytona die Feminina (-ə, e-, S. 83) bilden. [p. 48] Da jedoch der Zuwachs in der Formbildung meist nur eine Silbe ausmacht und auch die Feminina recht zahlreich sind, so erscheint die Mehrzahl der Wörter paroxytoniert, weshalb aus praktischen Gründen nach dem Vorgehen der Albanologen (G. Meyer) der Ton auf der vorletzten Silbe unbezeichnet bleibt. Im Gegischen und Toskischen ruht der Akzent auf derselben Silbe.
world_status: statement found in an open source
sweep_summary: Gheg Albanian is not in the catalog. this search of works with stress in the title returned two Glottolog records that are one work: Trommer 2013, Linguistic Inquiry 44(1):109-143 (doi 10.1162/LING_a_00121), which Glottolog files under gheg1238 but which describes Standard (Tosk-based) Albanian: n.1 states all data are in Standard Albanian orthography, its descriptive sources are Newmark et al. 1982, Camaj 1984, Buchholz & Fiedler 1987 and Agalliu et al. 2002, and the words Gheg/Tosk never appear. The article is closed access everywhere (OpenAlex/Unpaywall/Semantic Scholar: no OA copy; MIT Press Direct and Project MUSE bot-walled; no preprint on the author's Leipzig page per the Internet Archive 2025-12-09), but the 2021-08-03 Internet Archive copy of the publisher's own HTML page contains the complete text (minus image tableaux), which was saved and extracted to (HTML; OpenAlex record, the 2005 GLOW precursor abstract, and the author's page capture also. updated). Its statement (sec. 1, sec. 2.1): stem-bounded ultima/penult stress predictable from the final syllable of the base form (final if closed-with-full-vowel or a/i/u-final, penult if mid-vowel-final or closed schwa), retained unchanged under inflection, verbs stem-final, ~97% coverage. For Gheg this is other-variety evidence, relevant only through Pekmezi 1908's claim (already held by the project) that Gheg and Tosk stress the same syllable; the Gheg-specific first-hand sources remain Lowman 1932, Pisko 1896 and Weigand 1913 in the same folder. Side note for the parent: the tosk1239 record's high-priority works still to obtain (Trommer 2013 full text) is now obtained at the path above and can upgrade that record's deciding citation from the 2004 slides to the peer-reviewed article. all look-ups were done by automated download, direct download, the Internet Archive, Crossref, OpenAlex, Unpaywall and Semantic Scholar APIs. Nothing left to acquire for this language from this search of works with stress in the title.

new_statements.quote: Der Akzent ist unbeweglich; er ruht immer auf derselben Silbe in allen Formen und zum Teil auch Ableitungen eines Wortes: mál Berg, best. máli, gen. dat. plur. máleve [...] Seiner Stelle nach steht der Akzent in Grundwörtern auf der letzten Silbe und nur in ganz bestimmten Fällen auch auf der vorletzten. Diese letzteren betreffen Feminina auf -ë, -e (aus -jā = -jë) und -o: púnë (pu'n) Arbeit, núse Braut, víto Taube; Adjektiva, sowie überhaupt Wörter auf -ë [...] Alle übrigen Grundwörter und Suffixe sind oxytoniert [...] Im Gegischen und Toskischen ruht der Akzent auf derselben Silbe.
new_statements.translation: The accent is immobile; it always rests on the same syllable in all forms and in part also in the derivatives of a word: mál 'mountain', def. máli, gen.-dat. pl. máleve [...] As to its position, in base words the accent stands on the last syllable and only in quite specific cases on the penultimate. The latter concern feminines in -ë, -e (from -jā = -jë) and -o: púnë 'work', núse 'bride', víto 'dove'; adjectives, and in general words in -ë [...] All other base words and suffixes are oxytone [...] In Gheg and in Tosk the accent rests on the same syllable.
new_statements.citation: Pekmezi, Georg. 1908. Grammatik der albanesischen Sprache (Laut- und Formenlehre). Wien: Verlag des Albanesischen Vereines 'Dija'.
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Quote check: the Pekmezi 1908 Fraktur scanned is unusable, so I read the saved page scan and book pp. 47-48, sec. 22 'Akzent'). Every clause of the reported quote is on the page verbatim, with the [..] elisions covering only example lists: 'Der Akzent ist unbeweglich; er ruht immer auf derselben Silbe in allen Formen und zum Teil auch Ableitungen eines Wortes: mál Berg, best. máli, gen. dat. plur. máleve..'; 'Seiner Stelle nach steht der Akzent in Grundwoertern auf der letzten Silbe und nur in ganz bestimmten Faellen auch auf der vorletzten. Diese letzteren betreffen Feminina auf -ë, -e (aus -jā = -jë) und -o: púnë (pu'n) Arbeit, núse Braut, víto Taube; Adjektiva, sowie ueberhaupt Woerter a…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress is fixed on the stem (does not move under inflection): base words are stressed on their final syllable, except that words ending in unstressed -ë/-e/-o and a closed list of unstressed suffixes (-ës, -ën, -zë, -ur, -un, -të, -tas, -a) have penultimate stress, i.e. stress falls on the last full vowel of the stem; the position is identical in Gheg and Tosk. Weigand 1913 (South Gheg) adds that long and nasal vowels always carry the accent; Pisko 1896 (Shkodër Gheg) says most words are paroxytone in their full (suffixed) forms.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Pekmezi § 24 (p. 49) only ranks unstressed syllables by relative strength (the syllables immediately before and after the tonic are weakest); no secondary stress rule. Newmark 1982 (Standard Albanian) notes secondary stress on non-final stems of compounds.
new_statements.exceptions: Pekmezi p. 48: isolated Gheg/Tosk mismatches (aü/aj 'he', ńer-i/ńir-i 'man', ver-i 'north wind', taší/téš 'now', i vápëk/i vobékt 'poor', nepërkë, krëhërë/krąhën 'comb') attributed to sentence accent and analogy; because inflection usually adds one syllable and feminines are numerous, most word forms surface as paroxytone. Desnickaja 1968: South Gheg retracts stress to the penult in Turkish loans (téqe, káfe) where Tosk keeps final stress.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level accent of citation/inflected forms; Pekmezi treats Gheg and Tosk jointly with Gheg forms cited throughout; length contrasts occur only under stress (§ 23).
new_statements.identity_note: Pekmezi 1908 describes Albanian as a whole (alba1267 level) with Gheg and Tosk forms given side by side, and states explicitly that the accent falls on the same syllable in Gheg and Tosk. The two Gheg-only sources read here are Weigand 1913 = South Gheg of Durrës/Elbasan/Tirana (Glottolog Southern Gheg, within gheg1238) and Pisko 1896 = North(west) Gheg of Shkodër; both give only marking conventions consistent with Pekmezi's rule (default penult in full forms; long/nasal vowels always stressed). Desnickaja 1968 adds a Gheg-specific detail: penult stress in Turkish loans in South Gheg vs final in Tosk.

new_statements.quote: In Albanian, word forms lacking overt inflection (e.g., nominative indefinite nouns) have final stress if the final syllable is closed (1a) or ends in a nonmid vowel (1b–c), while stress falls on the penultimate syllable if the final syllable ends in a mid vowel (1d–e) (Bevington 1974, Trommer, to appear). In forms with inflectional affixes (e.g., accusative definite nouns), stress falls on the same syllable as in corresponding forms without overt inflection, even when the phonology would trigger a different stress position.
new_statements.citation: Trommer, Jochen. 2013. Stress Uniformity in Albanian: Morphological Arguments for Cyclicity. Linguistic Inquiry 44(1): 109-143. doi:10.1162/LING_a_00121
new_statements.locator: sec. 1, first paragraph (article opening, p. 109 of the print run; HTML capture carries no page breaks) and sec. 2.1
new_statements.reading: Stress in (Standard) Albanian sits on the last or the second-to-last syllable of the stem and is fixed there across the paradigm: the stem's final syllable is stressed when closed with a full vowel or ending in a/i/u, the penult when the final syllable ends in a mid vowel or is a closed schwa syllable; inflectional suffixes are never stressed and never shift stress; verbs are uniformly stem-final. This is a phonologically predictable, stem-bounded, right-edge, weight-plus-vowel-quality system covering about 97% of the lexicon per the author. It is a Standard (Tosk-based) Albanian description, not a Gheg one: the article never mentions Gheg or Tosk and cites all data in Standard Albanian orthography from standard-language grammars. For Gheg it is applicable only via Pekmezi 1908's statement (held by the project) that Gheg and Tosk stress the same syllable; the Gheg-specific first-hand statements remain Lowman 1932 (Shkoder: usually penult, fixed across inflection), Pisko 1896 and Weigand 1913, all already in this folder.

sources.note: Sec. 22 'Akzent' (pp. 47-48): accent expiratory (musical element strong in Gheg); immobile through all inflected forms; in base words on the last syllable, on the penult only in defined cases (feminines in -e/-ë/-o, words in -ë, listed unstressed suffixes); masculines and verbs oxytone, feminines paroxytone; 'Im Gegischen und Toskischen ruht der Akzent auf derselben Silbe'; sec. 23: length only under stress.

sources.citation: Desnickaja, A. V. 1968. Albanskij jazyk i ego dialekty. Leningrad: Nauka.
sources.note: Detailed Gheg dialect survey but no general word-stress rule; notes that Gheg long/nasal vowels are always stressed (p. 40), that Gheg diphthongs ue/ye/ie carry stress on the first element 'as generally in Gheg', and that South Gheg shifts stress in Turkish loans to the penult (téqe, káfe vs Tosk teqé, kafé; p. 221 ff.).

sources.note: Sec. 5 'Länge und Kürze. Betonung' (pp. 5-6): accent mark written only when the accent is NOT on the penultimate syllable; words with a long (or nasal) vowel left unmarked 'da dieser immer den Akzent trägt'; ë occurs in South Gheg only in unstressed syllables (p. 3). No fuller rule; verbs classed as stem-stressed vs ending-stressed (p. ~100).
